english: Why is your face red? I fought with the herdsmen of the other village. Did you fight over the spring? We fought over it, and blood was not shed. The elders settled it. Their herd drinks at dawn and our cattle drink in the evening. The elders are wise. Now sit, I will cook meat for you. Were the young men hurt? They were hurt and now they are lying down.
uncertain: h₂ḱh₃ént read as 3pl 'were hurt' (h₂eḱh₃- not yet checked)

english: Old man, wake up! The white cow is bellowing in the cowshed. Is she lying down? She lies and trembles. The cow's calf is being born. Bring fire and water quickly. I bring fire and water. What shall I do? Hold the cow's head and speak to her. Now it has come out. It lives.

How many cows came home, grandfather? Ten cows and the ox. The black one is not here. She is heavy with calf. She is still at the fence. Shall I go and look for the black one? Go, and take fire with you. Beasts walk about at night. Are you afraid? I am not afraid; the moon is shining brightly.

Sister-in-law, do we shear the sheep today? We shear them, because the sun is burning. Where is the comb? It lies at the door. Hold the ram's legs: it kicks. The wool is white and soft. I will spin it, and you will weave for your brother. In winter it warms.
uncertain: toy in 'bʰréh₂trey-kʷe toy' could be 'your brother' or 'for you'

english: Mother, the red yearling calf has stayed behind. Where did you see it? I saw it in the evening at the spring. The calf does not go away from its own mother cow. Look for it in the enclosure. I looked for it there and did not see it. Now let us go down to the river. Call the dog; it will find it. Come quickly. Look for the calf for us.

Father, the river has dried up. The cattle are thirsty and bellow. Now let us lead them to the meadow. Is the meadow far? It is far; we will walk two days. I call on Dyeus. Father Dyeus, may he rain on our fields. May Dyeus hear you.
